sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioners in O.P.(MV) No.196/2017 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kasaragod,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 27/03/2019.
The respondents herein are respondents 1 to 3 respectively in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioners, on 17/01/2016 at about 04:45 p.m., while the first claim petitioner was riding his bicycle along the road at the place by name Rahmath Nagar, car bearing registration no.KL-14/K-161 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of 2025:KER:72750 MACA NO. 577 OF 2020 which he sustained grievous injuries.
A sum of 5,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The claim petition was dismissed as against the first respondent/driver of the offending vehicle since no steps were taken against him.
The second respondent/owner of the offending vehicle remained ex parte.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
It was contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the first claim petitioner.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A6 were marked on the side of the claim petitioners.
No documentary evidence was produced by the third respondent/insurer.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending vehicle resulting in 2025:KER:72750 MACA NO. 577 OF 2020 the incident and hence awarded an amount of 81,750/-
together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioners have come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

sentences.text: 8. Heard both sides
9. The Award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioners - Extra nourishment
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that though an amount of 50,000/- was claimed, the Tribunal has not awarded any amount.

Hence,
reasonable amount may be awarded under this head.
9.1. The accident in this case occurred on 17/01/2016.

Hence, compensation at the rate of 400/-
per day for a period of 5 2025:KER:72750 MACA NO. 577 OF 2020 days can be awarded (400 x 5 =
2,000/-).
Future treatment 10.
Though an amount of 1,00,000/- was claimed, the Tribunal has not granted any amount under this head.

The learned counsel for the claim petitioners submitted that for removal of implant, an amount between 40,000/- to 1,00,000/- would be required and hence a reasonable amount may be awarded.
10.1.

Ext.A6 medical certificate produced reads thus:-
"Master Sinan E.K., Chengala (PO) was admitted under me on 17/01/2016 with left femur supra-condylar fracture of femur.
He was operated on 18/01/2016 with K-wire.
I have advised him rest for 4 months (four months).
After 4-6 months depending on union he will have to undergo another surgery to remove the implant.
That surgery would roughly cost around 10,000/- (ten thousand)"
(Emphasis supplied)
In the light of Ext.A6, an amount of 10,000/- is awarded under this head.
2025:KER:72750 MACA NO. 577 OF 2020 Attender's charge 11.
As the accident took place on 17/01/2016, compensation at the rate of 450/- per day for a period of 5 days can be granted (450 x 5 = 2,250/-).
Compensation for pain and suffering 12.
The materials on record show that the first claim petitioner had sustained displaced fracture (supra-condylar and comminuted) of left femur.
He was hospitalized for a period of 5 days.
Hence, I find that an amount of 40,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
Compensation for loss of amenities and conveniences of life 13.
Though no amount was claimed, the Tribunal has granted an amount of 20,000/- under this head.
However, taking into account the age of the first claim petitioner, I find that an amount of 30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
